summary: A first-person excerpt from a fiction book (labeled Book 14, part 50) in which the narrator describes retaliating against three mean girls at school. The narrator targets Rebecca with planted hair, Lyndsay with chocolate truffles, and Harper with a staged romance that ends in a disappointing poetry reading. The excerpt breaks off mid-sentence during the Harper section.
one_line: A fictional narrator recounts sabotaging three cruel schoolgirls, Rebecca, Lyndsay, and Harper, with planted hair, chocolate truffles, and a fake date.
key_facts: The narrator describes Rebecca as a girl most likely to succeed at making other people miserable, who was beautiful, smart, and had perfect timing with mean jokes.
The narrator collected hair matching Rebecca's hair color from the trash behind a hair salon and carried it in a baggie to leave clumps around.
The narrator jammed hair into Rebecca's hairbrush so she would think her hair was falling out when she brushed it.
The narrator sprinkled hair on the floor by Rebecca's locker every day for a week.
Rebecca started skipping school, and her Facebook timeline filled with hair-related trauma.
Rebecca still found hair clumps everywhere after the narrator had run out of the planted hair.
The narrator sabotaged Lyndsay by leaving chocolate truffles all over the place, knowing she would eat them and then hate herself.
The narrator later heard that Lyndsay had to go into a residential treatment program for eating disorders.
Harper was taken down through a fake romance with a university student she had met at a party.
The university student sent Harper Tweets that were funny and sweet and later exchanged texts with her containing heavy-breathing content.
Harper spent a fortune on pre-torn jeans and three new pairs of shoes before her special date.
The date was supposed to be an evening to hear an amazing band, but the venue turned out not to be a bar and instead hosted a poetry reading.
The narrator says the cute guy was at the poetry reading but acted like he didn't know Harper, and the excerpt ends mid-sentence.
